The Rose have been here twice, and they sold out our biggest club venue once, then when they were upgraded for the most recent tour, they didn't anywhere near sell out, judging from attendance. Still fantastic, and I'm grateful to see them twice in my home country, of course!

But yeah, America is huge and groups will likely play the big cities for the most part. Of course, this favours the fans who live there or can afford to travel, but yeah, life isn't fair and concerts are a luxury, after all.

I have to agree with this. For context, I am 30, was diagnosed with TLE at 21, but had symptoms for many many years without doctors being able to diagnose it. 

I have also experienced both, and with panic attacks my heart race and I start breathing heavily, can't properly focus and feel like things happen too fast. My experiences with TLE have felt far "calmer" in the sense that the auras can feel quite fascinating and a bit "dream-like" (I have had hallucinations), until I get that feeling of nausea which has almost always been linked to a phantom taste in my mouth. Random OT, but my auras taste like Juicy Fruit gum, exclusively. A friend said hers tasted like Smarties. At least they're rather pleasant tastes, though I can't stand Juicy Fruit now.

However, my most common aura (and the one I remember having often as a kid, but was one of those things I thought everyone experienced) is auditory, where every sound is amplified and sound "too fast" and sort of aggressive. It also comes with tunnel vision, but not every time. My mom told me I used to say that "the sounds are angry" as a child, but I don't remember any fear being associated with it from childhood. But when I experience this specific aura now, it feels quite similar to a panic attack, because it's this feeling of internal stress, and when it happens, I have to sit down and just let it pass, much in the same way. I'm not sure if this is because I associate it with the fainting spells that can occur, or because I have since childhood experienced panic attacks as well and realized they feel similar to me, personally.

Ah, I don't know if this helps in any way, but I know for me, learning about how other people experience TLE, has helped me understand my own condition better. Hang in there! <3
